title: Portuguese-from-Portugal wording in account update message
expected_behavior: Use natural Brazilian Portuguese spelling and phrasing.
actual_behavior: Response used 'actualizada' and 'Pode verificar a informação', which are not natural for pt-BR product messaging.
user_impact: Brazilian users may perceive the product as poorly localized or not intended for Brazil.
recommended_fix: Replace Portugal-oriented spelling and phrasing with pt-BR: 'Sua conta foi atualizada com sucesso. Você pode conferir as informações no seu perfil.'

title: False friend mistranslation of eventually
expected_behavior: Translate 'eventually' according to context, usually as 'por fim', 'com o tempo' or 'em algum momento'.
actual_behavior: Response translated 'eventually' as 'eventualmente', changing the intended meaning.
user_impact: Users may misunderstand timing, frequency or product behavior.
recommended_fix: Add false-friend checks for common EN/PT terms such as eventually, actually, currently, pretend and sensible.

title: US date and time format used for Brazilian locale
expected_behavior: Use Brazilian date and time conventions: DD/MM/YYYY and 24-hour format when appropriate.
user_impact: Brazilian users may misread the renewal date and time, especially in billing contexts.

title: Portugal-oriented subscription terminology
expected_behavior: Use Brazilian product terminology for account settings and subscriptions.
actual_behavior: Response used 'subscrição' and 'definições' instead of 'assinatura' and 'configurações'.
user_impact: Message is understandable but sounds translated for Brazilian users.
recommended_fix: Update terminology glossary and prefer 'assinatura', 'configurações' and 'cancelar' for pt-BR SaaS flows.}
